# Progressive and Multi-stage Training

Also called: Coarse-to-Fine Training, Stage-wise Optimization, Curriculum Learning for Gaussians

## Overview
Progressive and Multi-stage Training refers to a family of optimization strategies that decompose the training of 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) into sequential phases, each with distinct goals, active parameters, or supervision signals. It solves the problem of unstable convergence, geometric ambiguity, and slow detail acquisition inherent in single-stage, monolithic optimization [S1, 15018-multi-stage-training-with-pose-prediction.md, unofficial]. Unlike standard training, which optimizes all attributes simultaneously from initialization, these methods decouple coarse geometry establishment from fine appearance refinement, or separate pose estimation from geometry learning, to prevent error propagation and improve final rendering quality [7173-hybrid-coarse-to-fine-strategy.md, 15018-multi-stage-training-with-pose-prediction.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family operate on the Gaussian set $\mathcal{G}$ defined in [Densification Strategy](6234-densification-strategy.md). The core mechanism involves partitioning the optimization timeline into discrete stages $S_1, \dots, S_k$. Each stage $S_i$ is characterized by:
1.  **Parameter Freezing/Unfreezing:** A subset of Gaussian attributes (e.g., position $\mu$, scale $s$, SH coefficients $\mathbf{c}$) or model components (e.g., pose estimators, encoders) are frozen while others are updated [15018-multi-stage-training-with-pose-prediction.md].
2.  **Supervision Shift:** The loss function $\mathcal{L}$ changes across stages. Early stages may use geometric or coarse photometric losses, while later stages introduce high-frequency details (e.g., higher SH degrees) or additional constraints (e.g., depth, normal consistency) [7173-hybrid-coarse-to-fine-strategy.md, 17879-training-loop-with-mixed-losses-and-post-processing.md].
3.  **Curriculum or Progressive Exposure:** Inputs or sampling strategies evolve. For example, training may start with sparse voxel sampling or low-resolution views, progressing to dense, high-resolution supervision [12921-curriculum-learning-with-slice-and-voxel-supervision.md, 15162-free-view-training-fvt.md].

## Subtopics

### [Hybrid Coarse-to-Fine Strategy](7173-hybrid-coarse-to-fine-strategy.md)
Decouples initial coarse geometry placement from high-frequency appearance refinement. It solves unstable convergence in single-stage training by first optimizing basic position and scale to establish layout, then enabling Spherical Harmonics (SH) for view-dependent detail. It sets itself apart by explicitly freezing SH in Stage 1 and activating them in Stage 2, often combined with a consistency filter.

### [Training Objective and Densification](7448-training-objective-and-densification.md)
Defines a multi-stage approach for **MeshGS**, separating Gaussians into "tightly-bound" (constrained to a mesh) and "loosely-bound" (standard densification) subsets. It solves geometric inconsistency by applying distinct loss terms (normal consistency, scale regularization) and densification logic to the tightly-bound group, ensuring surface fidelity while allowing loose Gaussians to fill gaps.

### [Fine-tuning](9138-fine-tuning.md)
Refines an initial Gaussian representation (from SfM or feed-forward prediction) to achieve high-fidelity reconstruction. It sets itself apart by allowing dynamic densification and continuous parameter updates during the per-scene optimization phase, adapting the static initialization to minimize image-space error. Variants include generative prior fine-tuning (GPN) and multi-modal volume fine-tuning.

### [Curriculum Learning with Slice and Voxel Supervision](12921-curriculum-learning-with-slice-and-voxel-supervision.md)
Addresses instability in shear-warp rendering by combining sparse voxel sampling with structured slice-based sampling. It sets itself apart by explicitly aligning training supervision with the 2D slice structure of the renderer, starting with slice supervision for structural details and progressing to voxel supervision for global spatial guidance.

### [Multi-stage Training with Pose Prediction](15018-multi-stage-training-with-pose-prediction.md)
Addresses the instability of jointly optimizing camera poses and 3D Gaussian attributes. It solves the "chicken-and-egg" problem by segmenting training into: Stage 1 (coarse geometry/pose with ground-truth supervision), Stage 2 (pose-corrected refinement with frozen pose estimator), and Stage 3 (end-to-end pose-free fine-tuning). It sets itself apart by progressively unfreezing pose parameters to enable pose-free inference.

### [Free-View Training (FVT)](15162-free-view-training-fvt.md)
Disentangles generalizable 3DGS performance from the specific number of input views. It achieves this by training on long sequences with randomly sampled context views ($T=2$ to $8$) and supervising full-resolution renderings. It sets itself apart from fixed-view methods by enabling robust synthesis across broader view ranges regardless of input count.

### [Training Loop with Mixed Losses and Post-Processing](17879-training-loop-with-mixed-losses-and-post-processing.md)
Defines an iterative optimization step integrating photometric, depth, and regularization losses with a progressive SH degree schedule. It distinguishes itself by explicitly handling multi-modal supervision (RGB + Depth), appearance post-processing via bilateral grids, and visibility-aware optimizer stepping to improve convergence stability.

### [Training Loop with Structure-Aware Densification](22986-training-loop-with-structure-aware-densification.md)
Accelerates training by replacing reactive densification with a structure-aware strategy using precomputed frequency metrics. It solves slow convergence by ensuring Gaussians are split only where high-frequency details exist. It sets itself apart by using explicit frequency estimation rather than geometric thresholds, and from [Hybrid Coarse-to-Fine Strategy](7173-hybrid-coarse-to-fine-strategy.md) by integrating densification logic directly into the forward pass buffers.

#### Progressive Propagation Strategy
Introduces a progressive propagation strategy to expand the Gaussian cloud in a fronto-parallel manner, ensuring smooth expansion and better coverage [S1, unofficial].

#### Interleaved Densification
Alternates between spatial and temporal densification every 2 epochs to avoid Gaussians failing to reconstruct either motion or appearance detail [S2].

#### Two-Stage Training Scheme for FWD-U
A training strategy that decouples depth network initialization from full model training to improve stability and performance [S3].
*   **Step:** Stage 1: Construct RGB point clouds for each input view, project to target view, aggregate, and optimize depth network using photometric loss. Stage 2: Freeze/continue depth network and jointly train the entire model (spatial feature network, MLP, renderer, transformer, refinement module) [S3].
*   **Parameter:** Performance improvement of approximately 0.4 dB PSNR [S3].
*   **Pitfall:** Jointly training the depth network and other components from scratch causes instability [S3].

#### Two-Stage Triplane and MLP Training
*   **Step:** Stage 1: Jointly train triplanes and MLP on 500 randomly selected shapes (batch size 1 object, 500k occupancy points, 200 epochs, lr 1e-3). Stage 2: Freeze shared MLP, train triplane features for each object individually (batch size 200k points, 30 epochs, lr 1e-3) [S4].
*   **Parameter:** Triplane feature dimension: $128 \times 128 \times 32 \times 3$. Triplane initialization: normal distribution ($\sigma=0.1$). MLP: Fourier feature mapping (scale 1) + 3 FC layers (dim 128, ReLU) [S4].
*   **Number:** Stage 1 time: ~1 day on RTX 2080ti. Stage 2 time: 10 minutes per shape on RTX 2080ti [S4].

#### Continual Model Refinement
*   **Step:** Augment initial model with closer-up images (64 or 512) to simulate prolonged interaction. Optimize for up to 4000 iterations, including 400 iterations of densification [S5].
*   **Parameter:** Final Gaussian count grows to 20k–50k. Training speed: >500 iterations/sec [S5].
*   **Pitfall:** Improvement becomes marginal after 2000 iterations. Using foveated/undistorted views decreases quality by 5–10% [S5].
*   **Comparison:** Fixed foveation center vs. variable points yields <1% quality difference [S5].

#### Projection-Based Frequency Violation Metric
A densification trigger applying a three-channel anisotropic criterion where each Gaussian axis is evaluated against its own directional frequency content [S6].
*   **Number:** On Mip-NeRF360, $\eta^{(proj)}$ achieves PSNR 27.20 and LPIPS 0.203, compared to the scalar metric's PSNR 27.25 and LPIPS 0.197 [S6].
*   **Comparison:** Theoretically more precise than the scalar wavelength metric, but yields worse perceptual quality (LPIPS) in practice because it relies on accurate axis-direction alignment that is not yet optimized during training [S6].

## Background
The concept of multi-stage training in 3DGS originates from the observation that single-stage optimization often leads to suboptimal geometry initialization and unstable convergence, particularly when high-frequency details (SH coefficients) are introduced too early [7173-hybrid-coarse-to-fine-strategy.md]. The Hybrid Coarse-to-Fine Strategy was among the first to explicitly separate coarse geometry from fine appearance [S1, unofficial]. Subsequent works like MeshGS [7448-training-objective-and-densification.md] and FWD-U [S3] extended this to incorporate explicit geometric constraints (meshes, depth) in staged manners. The challenge of pose-geometry coupling led to multi-stage pose prediction methods [15018-multi-stage-training-with-pose-prediction.md], while curriculum learning approaches [12921-curriculum-learning-with-slice-and-voxel-supervision.md] adapted the concept to volumetric data. Recent variations focus on efficiency (Structure-Aware Densification [22986-training-loop-with-structure-aware-densification.md]) and generalization (Free-View Training [15162-free-view-training-fvt.md]).
